The monsoon trough with embedded Invest 92W to the southwest of the 
Marianas continues to push occasionally scattered showers into the 
region along with increasingly southerly winds. This disturbance is 
expected to keep its distance and keep the Marianas dry overall for 
the next few days, with the exception of increasing island effect 
showers and thunderstorms. Guam may receive slightly more rainfall 
due to its closer proximity to 92W. Light to gentle winds will slowly
drop off to light and variable winds tomorrow night. This will allow
island effect showers and thunderstorms to develop in the afternoon 
through Saturday for Guam, Tinian, and Saipan. Winds may even be 
light enough Thursday for Rota to receive island effect showers. 
Coverage will depend on how clear conditions are in the mornings. As
a shearline/cold front and the band of convergence near Chuuk
interact, this may increase the chance for precipitation over the 
Marianas Wednesday night. However, this remains uncertain so isolated
showers and thunderstorms remain in the forecast. Afterwards, 
overall shower coverage is expected to return to isolated over the 
weekend, with isolated thunderstorms returning at the end of the week
as Invest 93W potentially approaches the Marianas.

Marine...
Light to gentle southeasterlies will prevail across the region 
through early tonight, shifting south by midnight. Combined seas of 
4 to 5 feet are expected to remain fairly steady with a slight 
increase Wednesday possible depending on the monsoon surge to the 
southwest. Otherwise, seas look to drop Thursday night. The main 
swells are the dominant southwest swell, the weak easterly trade 
swell, and a weak southeast swell. A moderate risk of rip currents is
in effect for south and west facing reefs. A fourth weak, but very 
long period southeast swell is also possible sometime tomorrow. 
Therefore, east reefs will need to be monitored for the potential to 
reach a moderate risk of rip currents as soon as Wednesday night. 
Isolated thunderstorms are possible through at least Friday, causing 
a moderate risk of lightning along coastlines.

Tropical Systems...
A very broad, weak disturbance has begun to take shape within the 
monsoon trough north of Palau and Yap near 13N136E, now dubbed 
Invest 92W by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC). 92W is rated 
"sub-low", meaning it is not expected to develop into a significant 
tropical cyclone (a tropical depression) over the next few days, but 
will continue to be monitored for development. Himawari visible 
satellite imagery this afternoon shows an area of broad, flaring 
convection within the convergence along 92W's southern and eastern 
flank, associated with the monsoon pattern feeding into it. Moderate 
to locally heavy rainfall persisted over Yap through the morning, 
but is beginning to break up this afternoon. While showers are also
fairly patchy to the southwest near Palau, locally heavy rainfall 
will be possible at times through at least tonight as 92W shifts 
northwestward. Over the next few days, Invest 92W looks to gradually 
develop a very broad circulation over the Philippine Sea as it 
meanders northwest, potentially exiting west of Guam's Area of 
Responsibility (AOR) by the end of the week, and potentially as a 
tropical depression. Overall, 92W will help maintain a wet monsoon 
pattern over far western Micronesia for much of the remainder of the 
week.

Additionally, a weak disturbance is seen to the northeast of Majuro 
Atoll near 12N178E, now dubbed Invest 93W by JTWC as of this 
morning. 93W is also rated as a "sub-low", and development is not 
expected over the next few days. Latest scatterometry data depicts a 
small circulation here with 15 to 20 mph winds along its northern 
flank, and a small embedded area of 25 mph winds associated with 
nearby convection. There is another weak circulation nearby to its 
southwest, located southeast of Majuro near 4N174E. CIMSS 850mb 
vorticity analysis shows the stronger low-level vorticity is focused 
around 93W, and models support slight consolidation around this area 
over the next few days. At the same time, some of the vorticity near 
Majuro looks to shift westward and away, potentially slowing the 
development of Invest 93W somewhat as it meanders west- 
northwestward.

Eastern Micronesia...
Fairly dry conditions prevail across eastern Micronesia as a
doldrum-like pattern begins to set up. The heavy showers associated
with the broad southeastward convergence near Pohnpei and Kosrae,
south of the monsoon trough, are shifting farther west. Only patchy 
isolated to scattered showers remain, mainly between Majuro and 
Kosrae, and southwest of Kosrae and Pohnpei. Meanwhile, a pair of
weak surface circulations persist over the eastern RMI and northeast
of Majuro, but skies are partly cloudy with only isolated showers
